info.name: Ava API
info.description:
Multi-tenant Go API — auth, tenants with roles, and the onboarding flow engine.

## Getting started

1. `docker compose up -d postgres` then `make dev` (or `make run`).
2. Send **Auth › Register**, then verify the email (see that request's description for how to read the token out of the database locally).
3. Send **Auth › Login** — the access and refresh tokens are captured into collection variables automatically, and every protected request inherits them.

## How auth works here

User requests carry no `Authorization` header at all. Login sets **httpOnly cookies** (`ava_access`, `ava_refresh`) and Postman's cookie jar replays them, so the session simply works — and the tokens are never visible to scripts, which is the point. A session is scoped to **one tenant**. Login signs you into the tenant you used last; **Switch tenant** moves between them, revoking the current session and issuing a new one.

Hub requests are the exception: a device has no cookie jar, so those still send `Authorization: Bearer {{hubAccessToken}}`.

## Tokens that arrive by email

Email verification, password reset, and invitations all send a link. With no `RESEND_API_KEY` set, sending fails (logged as a warning) and the request still succeeds — read the token from Postgres, as each of those requests describes.

## Hubs and devices

A **hub** is the box in the home: it authenticates with the API through the RFC 8628 device grant (folder 6) and holds the credentials. **Devices** are what hang off it — they never authenticate, the hub reports them (folder 7). Requests that act as the hub carry the hub token rather than your user token; the collection tracks both.

## Rate limits

100 requests/minute per IP globally, 25/minute on auth endpoints. A throttled auth call returns 429 `auth_rate_limited`.

## Re-running

Folders 1–8 are safe to re-run. Folders 9 and 10 change the password, revoke the hub and log out, so a second full pass needs a fresh account or a reset database.

## Response envelope

Every response is `{ success, data, error: { code, message, details? } }`. Branch on `error.code`, not on the message text.

item.name: 2. Sign up and sign in
item.description: Run these in order. Register, verify the email (token comes from the database locally), then log in — the tokens are captured automatically and everything below inherits them.

request.description:
Creates the user, their tenant, and an owner membership in one transaction, then emails a verification link.

The slug must be lowercase alphanumeric words separated by hyphens. Login is blocked until the email is verified.

Marks the account verified. Single use — replaying the token returns 400.

The token arrives by email. Without a Resend API key nothing is sent, so read it straight from the database:

```
docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U ava -d ava_db -tA \
  -c "select token from tokens where type='email_verification' and used_at is null order by created_at desc limit 1"
```
Always answers 200, whether or not the address exists, and issues no new token for an already-verified account.

Signs in and sets the session cookies. A user who belongs to several tenants is signed into the one they used last (or their first, on a first login) — there is no selection step. Use **Switch tenant** to move between them.

item.name: 6. Hubs
item.description: Pairing a hub with a tenant using the RFC 8628 device authorization grant — the flow a TV app uses. Run these in order: request a code (as the hub), activate it (as the human), then poll (as the hub) to collect tokens.

request.description:
The hub calls this on first boot and shows the user_code on screen. Saves device_code and user_code to collection variables so the next two requests can act as the hub and the human.

`device_code` and `user_code` are RFC 8628 field names — the protocol's vocabulary, not the domain's. The thing being registered is a hub.

exec: console.log('Activate at ' + d.verification_uri + ' with code ' + d.user_code);

request.description: What the human does on their phone. Authenticated as a tenant member — the hub joins **their** tenant, which is why no tenant id appears in the body.

The hub polls this until a human approves. Before approval: 400 `authorization_pending`. Faster than the advertised interval: 429 `slow_down`. Denied: 403. Expired: 400 `expired_token`.

On success it saves the hub's access and refresh tokens.
Rotates the pair. The previous refresh token dies immediately, exactly like the user-side refresh.
Sent by the hub on a timer, using the **hub** token rather than a user token. Updates last_seen_at.
Hubs paired to the caller's tenant.
Everything this hub has reported.

item.name: 7. Devices
item.description: Devices hang off a hub and never authenticate themselves. Two writers: the hub owns kind, status and state; the user owns the name.

request.description:
Written by the **hub**, not a user. Full-list reconciliation: anything absent from the payload is marked offline rather than deleted, so ids and history survive a flaky sync.

The upsert touches kind, status, last_seen_at and state — never `name`, so a user's rename is not clobbered on the next sync.
Every device in the tenant, across all hubs. Read with a user token.

item.name: 8. Invitations
item.description: Accepting an invite is unauthenticated — the token is the credential. Invite someone from folder 4 first, then read the token out of the database.

request.description:
Activates a pending membership.

The invite token is emailed. Read it from the database with:

```
docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U ava -d ava_db -tA \
  -c "select invite_token from tenant_memberships where status='invited' order by created_at desc limit 1"
```

item.name: 9. Password
item.description:
⚠️ Ordered last on purpose. Change password swaps the password used by the Login request above, and Reset password revokes the caller's sessions in EVERY tenant, so anything after it needs a fresh login.

⚠️ These mutate the account: after Change password, the Login request in folder 2 no longer matches the password in its body. Re-running the whole collection wants a fresh account (change the email in Register, or drop the database volume).

request.description: Requires the current password. Unlike a reset, this does not revoke sessions.

Always answers 200 so accounts cannot be enumerated.

The token arrives by email. Without a Resend API key nothing is sent, so read it straight from the database:

```
docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U ava -d ava_db -tA \
  -c "select token from tokens where type='password_reset' and used_at is null order by created_at desc limit 1"
```
Consumes the token and revokes the user's sessions in every tenant, not just the current one.

item.name: 10. Teardown
item.description: ⚠️ Ordered last on purpose: each of these revokes something the rest of the collection depends on. Revoking the hub kills the hub token used by folder 7; logging out kills the user token used by everything else.

request.description: Owner or admin only. The hub's next heartbeat gets 401 and its refresh is refused, so it drops its stored credentials and asks for a new activation code.
Revokes this session only. The access token stops working immediately.
Revokes every session the caller has in the current tenant. Other tenants are unaffected.
